> Status: draft. Match barcodes, genome build, assay inputs, and reference labels to the study.

The cells align RNA counts, ATAC counts, and metadata before building a paired
Seurat object. They then run QC, WNN, and peak-to-gene linkage. WNN builds
multimodal neighborhoods; it does not correct batch effects.

## 1. Match RNA, ATAC, and metadata cells

The two count matrices have features in rows and cells in columns. The metadata
table has `cell_id` and `sample_id`.

```{r}
library(Seurat)
library(Signac)
library(qs2)
library(readr)

rna_counts <- qs2::qs_read("input/rna_counts.qs2")
atac_counts <- qs2::qs_read("input/atac_peak_counts.qs2")
metadata <- readr::read_tsv("input/cell_metadata.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)
annotation <- qs2::qs_read("input/gene_annotation.qs2")
fragments_path <- "input/fragments.tsv.gz"
stopifnot(all(c("cell_id", "sample_id") %in% names(metadata)))
stopifnot(!anyNA(metadata$cell_id), !anyDuplicated(metadata$cell_id))
stopifnot(file.exists(fragments_path), file.exists(paste0(fragments_path, ".tbi")))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(colnames(rna_counts)), !anyDuplicated(colnames(atac_counts)))

all_cells <- unique(c(colnames(rna_counts), colnames(atac_counts), metadata$cell_id))
cell_alignment <- data.frame(
  cell_id = all_cells,
  in_rna = all_cells %in% colnames(rna_counts),
  in_atac = all_cells %in% colnames(atac_counts),
  in_metadata = all_cells %in% metadata$cell_id
)
cells <- intersect(intersect(colnames(rna_counts), colnames(atac_counts)), metadata$cell_id)
stopifnot(length(cells) > 0)
rna_counts <- rna_counts[, cells, drop = FALSE]
atac_counts <- atac_counts[, cells, drop = FALSE]
metadata <- metadata[match(cells, metadata$cell_id), , drop = FALSE]
rownames(metadata) <- metadata$cell_id

fragment_object <- Signac::CreateFragmentObject(path = fragments_path,
                                                 cells = cells,
                                                 validate.fragments = TRUE)
chromatin_assay <- Signac::CreateChromatinAssay(
  counts = atac_counts, sep = c(":", "-"), genome = "hg38",
  annotation = annotation, fragments = fragment_object,
  min.cells = 1, min.features = 0
)
object <- Seurat::CreateSeuratObject(counts = rna_counts, assay = "RNA",
                                     meta.data = metadata, min.features = 0)
object[["ATAC"]] <- chromatin_assay
stopifnot(identical(colnames(object[["RNA"]]), colnames(object[["ATAC"]])))
object[["percent.mt"]] <- Seurat::PercentageFeatureSet(object, assay = "RNA",
                                                       pattern = "^MT-")
object <- Signac::NucleosomeSignal(object, assay = "ATAC")
object <- Signac::TSSEnrichment(object, assay = "ATAC", fast = TRUE)
qc <- object[[]]
object$qc_pass <- with(qc,
  !is.na(nFeature_RNA) & !is.na(nCount_RNA) &
    is.finite(percent.mt) & is.finite(nCount_ATAC) &
    is.finite(nucleosome_signal) & is.finite(TSS.enrichment) &
    nFeature_RNA >= 200 & nCount_RNA >= 500 & percent.mt <= 20 &
    nCount_ATAC >= 1000 & nucleosome_signal <= 1.5 & TSS.enrichment >= 6
)
print(table(object$sample_id, object$qc_pass, useNA = "ifany"))
VlnPlot(object, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"),
        group.by = "sample_id", ncol = 3, pt.size = 0)
VlnPlot(object, features = c("nCount_ATAC", "nucleosome_signal", "TSS.enrichment"),
        group.by = "sample_id", ncol = 3, pt.size = 0)
object <- subset(object, subset = qc_pass)
```

Use a matching genome build for peaks, fragments, annotation, and any later
sequence resources.

## 2. Build RNA and ATAC representations and WNN clusters

```{r}
object <- Seurat::NormalizeData(object, assay = "RNA")
object <- Seurat::FindVariableFeatures(object, assay = "RNA", nfeatures = 2000)
object <- Seurat::ScaleData(object, assay = "RNA",
                            features = Seurat::VariableFeatures(object, assay = "RNA"))
object <- Seurat::RunPCA(object, assay = "RNA", npcs = 30,
                         reduction.name = "pca_rna")

object <- Signac::RunTFIDF(object, assay = "ATAC")
object <- Signac::FindTopFeatures(object, assay = "ATAC", min.cutoff = "q0")
object <- Signac::RunSVD(object, assay = "ATAC", n = 50,
                         reduction.name = "lsi_atac")
Signac::DepthCor(object, reduction = "lsi_atac")

object <- Seurat::FindMultiModalNeighbors(
  object,
  reduction.list = list("pca_rna", "lsi_atac"),
  dims.list = list(1:30, 2:30),
  k.nn = 20,
  knn.graph.name = "wknn",
  snn.graph.name = "wsnn",
  weighted.nn.name = "weighted.nn"
)
object <- Seurat::RunUMAP(object, nn.name = "weighted.nn",
                          reduction.name = "wnn.umap", seed.use = 1)
object <- Seurat::FindClusters(object, graph.name = "wsnn",
                               resolution = 0.5, random.seed = 1)
DimPlot(object, reduction = "wnn.umap", group.by = "seurat_clusters", label = TRUE)
```

Inspect the ATAC depth correlation before choosing LSI dimensions. WNN does not
remove technical differences between samples.

## 3. Estimate peak-to-gene links

The coordinate object is a `GRanges` with the same genome build as the peak
assay. Links are statistical associations, not proof of regulation.

```{r}
gene_coordinates <- qs2::qs_read("input/gene_coordinates.qs2")
object <- Signac::LinkPeaks(
  object,
  peak.assay = "ATAC",
  expression.assay = "RNA",
  expression.slot = "data",
  peak.slot = "counts",
  gene.coords = gene_coordinates,
  distance = 500000,
  min.cells = 10
)
links <- Signac::Links(object[["ATAC"]])
```

## 4. Transfer labels from an RNA reference (optional)

GeneActivity is derived from accessibility; it is not measured RNA. Enable
this cell only with a compatible labeled RNA reference. Seurat uses CCA to
find shared structure across RNA and gene activity, then can use ATAC LSI to
weight predictions ([Seurat workflow](https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/seurat5_atacseq_integration_vignette)).

```{r}
#| eval: false

reference <- qs2::qs_read("input/rna_reference.qs2")
reference_label <- "cell_type"
stopifnot(reference_label %in% names(reference[[]]))
reference <- Seurat::NormalizeData(reference, assay = "RNA")
reference <- Seurat::FindVariableFeatures(reference, assay = "RNA", nfeatures = 2000)
transfer_features <- Seurat::VariableFeatures(reference, assay = "RNA")
reference <- Seurat::ScaleData(reference, assay = "RNA", features = transfer_features)
gene_activity <- Signac::GeneActivity(object, assay = "ATAC",
                                      features = transfer_features)
object[["ACTIVITY"]] <- SeuratObject::CreateAssay5Object(counts = gene_activity)
object <- Seurat::NormalizeData(object, assay = "ACTIVITY")
object <- Seurat::ScaleData(object, assay = "ACTIVITY",
                            features = rownames(object[["ACTIVITY"]]))
anchors <- Seurat::FindTransferAnchors(
  reference = reference, query = object,
  reference.assay = "RNA", query.assay = "ACTIVITY",
  features = intersect(transfer_features, rownames(object[["ACTIVITY"]])),
  reduction = "cca", dims = 1:30
)
predictions <- Seurat::TransferData(
  anchorset = anchors,
  refdata = setNames(reference[[reference_label, drop = TRUE]], colnames(reference)),
  weight.reduction = object[["lsi_atac"]],
  dims = 2:30
)
object <- Seurat::AddMetaData(object, metadata = predictions)
```

Review prediction scores and reference compatibility; there is no universal
confidence cutoff.

## 5. Save the object and links

```{r}
dir.create("output", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
qs2::qs_save(object, "output/multiome_analysis.qs2")
readr::write_tsv(as.data.frame(links), "output/peak_gene_links.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(cell_alignment, "output/multiome_cell_alignment.tsv")
```
